(4) VMT Projections and Emission Estimates
Our last concern arises from the lack of data to substantiate several claims made in the DEIS relative to regionwide VMT and emissions. As evidenced by Table 4-1 of the Metcalf & Eddy Air Quality Analysis, total VMT in the project area is expected to increase significantly over the no-build by 1990/2000. However, this is assigned minor importance because, "increased vehicle travel within the impact area will be balanced by a reduction in travel in other sections of the Metropolitan Boston area." Despite acknowledgement that the discussion of VMT projections on pages II-5-68 to II-5-69 of the DEIS is qualitative, we are not convinced that VMT in the Boston AQCR will indeed stabilize or decrease by 1990/2000. More importantly, even if VMT were to remain constant or decrease with implementation of any of the "Build" plans, it does not necessarily follow that regional emissions would also remain constant or decrease. The variation of emission rates with speed makes clear that, in terms of emissions, all VMT are not equal.
In short, additional arguments would seem to be warranted to support the contention that the proposed project will not adversely affect total <u>regional</u> emissions. Also, it is unclear to us why the emission estimates are predicted to be identical for 1990 and 2000. Realization of the full effectiveness of the Federal Motor Vehicle Emission Control Program together with gradually increasing VMT would seem to suggest that emissions should be on the rise between 1990 and 2000. Clarification of why emissions should (or should not) be equal in 1990 and 2000 would thus also be greatly appreciated.
In closing, it will as always be necessary that the proposed development comply with all of the Department of Environmental Quality Engineering's "Regulations as Amended for the Control of Air Pollution in the Metropolitan Boston Air Pollution Control District."
Please do not hesitate to contact this office if you should have any questions relative to any of the above.
